failedFirst: what the data holds > the things drawn and the links written between them: never a schema’s own things, nor a guess
what the data holds > the formats are told from the image formats, and a format no export writes is refused
a GQL block > names its graph, says where it came from in a comment, and writes one thing or link to a line
a GQL block > an id that is not a name, or is a word the profile keeps, is written in full under a name of its own
a GQL block > a line break in the note’s path never starts a line of code
CSV > one table: a header naming each property with the kind of its values, a row for each thing, then each link
CSV > an empty text is quoted, so it is told from a property the row does not have
CSV > a text a spreadsheet would run as a formula is guarded by an apostrophe, and read back without it
GraphML > a directed graph named as the graph is, with a key for each property and the kind of its values
GraphML > XML’s marks, a carriage return and spaces at either end are written so XML reads them back as written
GraphML > a text holding a character XML cannot hold is refused, naming the thing and the property: nothing is lost
the companion note > of an image split across pages, shows every page in order and says how many there are
the data, and an image across pages > the data is named as an image is, with its own ending, and gets no companion note: that links an image
the data, and an image across pages > a PNG split across pages names each page, in order, after the one name, and its companion note after that
the data, and an image across pages > a long name stays within 200 bytes with its .part, whatever its ending and however many pages
the data exports > the data is offered as a GQL block, as CSV and as GraphML
the data exports > the whole diagram’s data reads back, in each format, into the very things and links of the graph
the data exports > a view’s data is the things in the view and the links between them, with or without its faded context
the data exports > every value the profile reads comes back as itself: texts, numbers, truth values, days and instants
the data exports > a graph too large to draw still exports its data whole, and each format reads back the same
an image too large for one sharp PNG > is split across pages, each sharp and within the pixels allowed, together covering the image once
an image too large for one sharp PNG > an image that fits is one page, the whole of it; a wide one is split into columns only, a tall one into rows
an image too large for one sharp PNG > an image of fractional size is covered to its edge, the last page of each row and column the rest
an image too large for one sharp PNG > pages too small to read, or too many of them, are no split at all: the image is refused as too large
an image too large for one sharp PNG > each page is the image cut to its part: the same drawing, with its own size and view box
the data > is exported as a GQL block, as CSV and as GraphML, each reading back into the graph’s things and links
the data > of a view holds only the view’s things and the links between them, even with its faded context chosen
the data > of a graph too large to draw is still exported whole, with no layout asked for
a PNG too large for one sharp image > is split across pages, each within the pixels allowed and at twice natural size, named in order
a PNG too large for one sharp image > a page that cannot be written leaves none of them: every page written is taken away again
